works.title: Fido
works.medium: Polished Stainless Steel, Raspberry Pi 5, Diaphragm Pumps, Silicone Tubing, 3D-Printed Housing, YOLO11 Pose Detection, Loonen Bottles
works.description:
Designing Emerging Technologies, University of California, Berkeley
Fido is a speculative, fiduciary hydration system that assigns the decision to dispense water or alcohol to artificial intelligence. Built with two reservoirs, a pump system, and a camera-linked onboard computer, Fido treats the body as input and hydration as output. To receive a drink, users must complete the One-Leg Stand field sobriety test. The project asks what it means to outsource agency to systems designed to care on our behalf.

works.title: Painting to Dance With
works.medium: Canvas, steel, pine wood, various tools, Elmer's glue, India ink, oil, acrylic, graphite, colored pencil, Sharpie, dye-based ink, enamel
works.description:
2025 BA Thesis Exhibition: ALL WALLS FALL, The University of Chicago. Also selected for Festival of the Arts 2025 Winter Gallery, vestige, a student-selected and student-run exhibition at the University of Chicago.
Painting to Dance With emerged through an iterative conversation with materials, form, and digital tools. The work began as an abstraction of intuition, layered through experiments in scale, speed, symbolism, and rhythm. Up close, the surface reveals dense traces of human mark-making: footprints, hidden messages, small references, and accumulated gestures. From a distance, those details reorganize into a larger field of movement, inviting the viewer into a dance of approach and retreat.

works.title: Spaghetti0s
works.medium: Sharpie, Watercolor, & Graphite on Medium Density Fiberboard
works.description:
The University of Chicago
Spaghetti0s features a depiction of Chef Boyardee wielding an AK-47 and smoking a cigar. The composition is filled with fractal-like images that shift across various scales, guiding the viewer through a series of visual transitions where explicit shapes dissolve into implicit ones. As lines cross between scenes, they blur distinctions, creating a dynamic interplay of forms.

works.title: Trays
works.description:
The University of Chicago
In Trays, 20 cafeteria lunch trays function as containers for an eclectic assortment of found objects, each meticulously arranged to resemble food. The work explores the tension between container and contents: trays associated with nourishment, childhood routine, and institutional order instead hold items that are strange, absurd, and often harmful if consumed.
